history.text: It refers to antenatal care in the antenatal period.

latestLiveReplies.text: Antenatal means before birth, during pregnancy. So antenatal care is the care you get while you’re pregnant. [1]

latestLiveReplies.question: What does continuity of midwifery care actually mean? Please explain in plain words.
latestLiveReplies.review: Explain the concept directly in everyday words, with a relevant citation; no catalogue of studies or birth-plan recommendation.

sources.title: CG190 Intrapartum care for healthy women and babies: Full guideline Addendum 190.2

latestLiveReplies.text: Continuity of midwifery care means the same midwife, or a small known team, looks after you through pregnancy, birth and after the baby is born, instead of you meeting lots of different people [1][2][3].

limitations: One intermediate midwifery definition was withheld by the review gate. The latest retest produced a clear cited definition; the exact cause of the earlier rejection was not captured.
The review remains probabilistic and can withhold an answer. New diagnostic logs contain only fixed check names and counts, never private text or source URLs.
These checks verify response behaviour and display, not independent clinical approval of every claim or availability of every external source page.
The old exact dissatisfaction fallback remains only when no original question is available; criticism with clear conversation context now uses that context.
